review_notes: Reviewed all 108 lines of the target and the relevant related sources, especially PrincipalSeg.cocone, Set.principalSegIio, HasIterationOfShape, PreservesWellOrderContinuousOfShape, TransfiniteCompositionOfShape, Set.Ici.isSuccLimit_coe, HasColimit/IsColimit, and Set.Ici.subtype_functor_final. The central class IsWellOrderContinuous asserts that the specific canonical cocone over Set.Iio m with point F.obj m is a colimit at every successor-limit m. This is not the same concept as HasIterationOfShape, which asserts only the existence of colimits of the relevant shapes, nor HasColimit, which does not fix the cocone or apex. The extraction/specialisation definitions and the Nat/Fin vacuous instances are new API or special cases, not competing copies of an existing Mathlib concept. The local finality argument in restriction_setIci is a proof ingredient; it is not a new duplicate finality declaration. I did not find a justified same-concept duplication under the rubric. I could not execute Lean, and the remaining uncertainty is limited to potential proof/API refactoring (for example, generic Archimedean instances) rather than duplication of an existing concept.
